query:
Industry: photography gallery
Client brief: A contemporary photography gallery called Intervals. Black and white only, Helvetica only, no animation. Make historical photographs the main experience, with an exhibition introduction, selected works, artist information and an exhibition enquiry. No invented awards or sales claims.
Audience: photography enthusiasts and collectors
Primary action: view the photographs and enquire about an exhibition
Heading font: Helvetica
Body font: Helvetica
Brand colours: #FFFFFF, #111111, #666666
No animation.
No coloured accents.
No invented awards.

matched_industry.name: Creative Portfolios & Independent Makers
matched_industry.layout_archetype: Curated Work Index + Deep Case Study Monograph
matched_industry.first_viewport_priority: Clear practitioner identity, selected shipped works, and availability status

typography_pairing.mood: The brief's own type (Helvetica); scale and roles from literata-inter

palette.notes: Brief colours #FFFFFF, #111111, #666666 lead: #FFFFFF is the ground; #666666 as accents; #111111 as surfaces and deep tones, never accents | base Town-hall limestone with notice blue and stamp red

conversion_trust_elements: Role, timeline, and shipped impact per project
matched_industry.motion_language: Hover-linked project preview planes, FLIP route continuity

category_cliches: Black-and-white with a single gold accent
Huge thin serif + letter-spaced caps everywhere
Full-screen hero video with centred logo
distinctiveness.instruction: Subject first: list the objects, tools and moments a visitor actually sees in this business (a bakery: loaves, the oven, flour; an optician: frames, lenses, the test chart). The first screen must show the most characteristic of them as authored art at scale, so a stranger can name the business with the text covered. Then write down 3 concrete references from the brand's own world (local architecture, craft traditions, signage, landscape, the material itself) and derive palette, pattern, and type voice from them. The clichés below are generic *treatments* (layouts, kits, palettes), not the subject's own objects: avoid the treatments, never the subject.

matched_styles.name: Kinetic Editorial Showcase
characteristics: Choreographed display typography with SplitText mask reveals
Scroll-synchronized case study pinning and smooth image scale transitions
Tactile magnetic triggers with instant reduced-motion static fallback

matched_styles.name: Spatial WebGL & Interactive 3D Stage
characteristics: Demand-rendered or viewport-throttled Three.js / R3F canvas with PBR lighting or custom shaders
Accessible semantic HTML overlay that remains 100% usable when WebGL is disabled or reduced-motion is active
Synchronized camera keyframes driven by scroll progress or pointer parallax
avoid_when: Content-heavy documentation or low-power utility forms

directions.title: Direction A — Creative Portfolios & Independent Makers (Full-Bleed Stage)
directions.layout_composition: Full-bleed stage for the photography gallery: the complete photograph fills the first screen edge to edge with the headline set into its quiet area; later sections cut between the artist and collection caption and the selected works at full width; 'view the photographs and enquire about an exhibition' stays docked and usable at every scroll position. Structure: one subject image edge to edge, headline in its quiet area, full-width cuts, docked action. Knobs: density standard; span irregularity medium; accent on the primary action only. Mobile: the image crops to a 4:5 focal point chosen by hand; the headline moves under it, never over a busy area
directions.visual_identity: Cinematic contrast: Helvetica at stage scale over Helvetica; palette brand-ffffff-111111-666666-on-civic-limestone (light ground): brief colours #ffffff, #111111, #666666 lead: #ffffff is the ground; #666666 as accents; #111111 as surfaces and deep tones, never accents; real photography or drawn art of the subject, never stock; corners: square corners (0) on cards, buttons and images (sharp-0); body 1rem (16px) minimum, labels and captions 0.75rem (12px) minimum

material.build: Rendered 3D objects of the trade, lit and shadowed, as the main visuals.

labels.build: Italic labels in the display face, set like captions in a book.

motion.build: Micro motion only: hover, focus and press states (150-200ms), no scroll choreography; signature: underline-sweep (CSS transitions). Reduced motion: under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce every effect is replaced by its final state; all content stays visible and readable.

motion_techniques.build: Link underlines sweep in on hover and focus, 180ms.

motif.build: Ruled frame: every chapter opens on a hairline rule with a short thick start segment, drawn from the trim lines of the complete photograph; figures and captions hang from the rule, which never crosses media.

button.build: Primary: solid accent fill, 48px tall with 24px side padding, radius 2px, label at medium weight; hover deepens the fill one step (150ms), press sinks it 1px, and keyboard focus shows a 2px accent ring offset 3px. restraint: No eyebrow or kicker labels above headings, and no tiny tracked caps anywhere.
No monospace face: figures use the body face's tabular numerals.

workflow_guidance: ROTATION: tell the user in one line before dealing: The last 12 runs used atelier-minimalism 7 times, swiss-editorial-grid 7 times, crisp-product-workbench 6 times, kinetic-editorial 6 times; this run picks from {hero-question-of-the-day, hero-headline-wraps-object, hero-ruled-ledger-poster}.

BRIEF FONTS: the brief names its own type (Helvetica). Build every direction's type system from these (display and body roles among them; a mono role only where the restraint allows one); the direction pairings below are fallbacks only.
BRIEF COLOURS: the brief names its own colours (#FFFFFF, #111111, #666666). Use them as the palette in every direction (check WCAG pairs); the direction palettes below are fallbacks only.

Mode A (New Website): the user's prompt wins over everything here. The 3 directions are structural raw material (layout, content treatment, dials), not finished looks; the visual world comes from art direction.

DISTINCTIVENESS: Read `distinctiveness` first. If `match_confidence` is `none` or `weak`, the industry profile is only a fallback; build the visual world from the brief's place and material cues instead, and do not ship any listed category cliché unless the brief asks for it.

ART DIRECTION (load `skills/layoza-art-direction`): commit to ONE specific world. Derive the world from far (place, notation, print traditions), keep the subject up close (the trade's object as the signature interaction, at scale), rule out the category reflex and its obvious opposite, and put the visitor's real action in the first viewport. Let colour own whole sections. Decide motion and tools per design; nothing is mandatory.

ENGINEERING LESSONS: sticky headers need `html { scroll-padding-top: <header height + 1rem> }` (WCAG 2.4.11); web fonts need metric-adjusted fallback `@font-face` (size-adjust / ascent-override) or the font swap re-wraps headings and fails CLS; scroll reveals must end visible.

HERO: Layoza does not fix the first-screen composition; you choose it, from the subject and the brief. The directions suggest centred / object-wrap / poster (each with its reason in `rationale`), and the dealt hero mechanic is one fit for that composition, not the only one. Give the three directions three different first screens, do not default to headline-left / visual-right (a split needs a stated reason), and record `HERO:` with the reason in `.layoza/direction.md`.
TYPE & LEADING: Keep multi-line display headings at `line-height >= 1.0` so ascenders and descenders never collide.

LAYOUT SAFETY: Keep short header links/buttons on one line (`white-space: nowrap`), give side-by-side heading columns >= 16px of clear space, collapse multi-column grids before gaps exceed the viewport, and size any <canvas> from a fixed-size container with devicePixelRatio capped at 2.
Verify in a real browser with `layoza qa <file-or-url>` (1440/768/375): it measures contrast, overflow, clipping, nav, scroll reveals, and lab Core Web Vitals; fix every error.

DIRECTIONS: render three materially different compositions with identical factual content and available assets at desktop and phone sizes. Compare the actual renders for hierarchy, typography, image integration, clarity and full-page rhythm. Choose with reasons as the designer unless the user asked to choose. Persist candidates, screenshot evidence and visible tradeoffs with review_design; never invent user approval. Library deals are starting material, not mandatory shapes or a substitute for art direction.

PAGE SHAPE: each direction's `page_shape` is a set of suggestions, not orders. Decide every axis (hero frame, flow, section heads, ground, material, labels, motion level and tools) from this brief's facts; keep a suggestion only when it serves your concept, and record each decision with its reason in .layoza/direction.md. Axes in `pinned_by_prompt` follow the user's words; whatever you choose stays unique against the ledger.

FORM: for each page or section answer narrative role, viewing distance, visual temperature, content capacity and visual motif before styling it; at delivery add one line per section saying which content the form came from.

COPY: specific nouns from the brief, no startup clichés, no invented metrics, reviews or logo walls (use honest placeholders such as `[customer quote — to supply]`), and call-to-action verbs taken from what the visitor actually does.

SELF-CRITIQUE before QA: score philosophy, hierarchy, execution, specificity, restraint, variety from 1 to 5; any score below 3 means revise first. Put the stamp `/* layoza · direction: <A|B|C> · structure: <style_family> · hero: <hero id> · palette: <palette id> · type: <type id> · critique: P4 H4 E4 S4 R4 V4 */` as the first line of the main CSS (your direction, structure, hero, palette, type and scores).
LOOK LEDGER: steered away from 36 look(s) in this project's last 12 run(s) (.layoza/looks.jsonl); 28 slot repeat(s) remain (see `uniqueness`). Pass ledger=false (CLI --no-ledger) to ignore it.

concepts.title: Direction B — Creative Portfolios & Independent Makers (Salon Hang)
concepts.composition: Photography gallery as a salon hang: one wall of framed pieces at different sizes, the complete photograph largest at eye height; each frame has a wall label; the artist and collection caption and the selected works as further walls; 'view the photographs and enquire about an exhibition' on the wall label. Structure: a wall of framed pieces hung at different sizes, each labelled. Knobs: density standard; span irregularity high; accent on the primary action only. Mobile: the wall becomes a single column of frames in hanging order
concepts.why_this_subject: Salon Hang for "photography gallery" (showcase surface): many pieces seen together in one wall tell the story better than one at a time. Type Helvetica / Helvetica (the brief's own type (helvetica); scale and roles from albert-sans-solo) for an expressive voice, tagged civic like the brief. Palette brand-ffffff-111111-666666-on-archive-stone on a light ground, tagged civic like the brief. First screen: object-wrap composition (no fitting layered hero for this trade, so the direction follows the dealt hero hero-headline-wraps-object), hero material photo, look family luxury-sparse, corners arched. Motion flavour (tier and tools follow page_shape.motion): pieces come forward on focus. Brand first: palette built around the brief's colours (#FFFFFF, #111111, #666666). Brand first: Helvetica is a commercial face: self-host it under the brand's own licence; it is not linked to a free CDN. Brand first: type built from the brief's fonts (Helvetica). Other structures that fit this slot: Split Studio, Pin-Board Collage, Object Study, Irregular Work Grid.

creative_workspace.selection: Render the three concepts with identical real content and available assets. Pick the clearest, most expressive, subject-specific composition; record the decision and visible tradeoffs with review_design. Familiar controls may be reused when they serve the task.
creative_workspace.novelty: A supporting signal, never a reason to change a working brand or navigation pattern
creative_workspace.design_gate: Browser defects and recorded process only. Exceptional design requires reviewing the actual renders, not passing a numeric checker.

client_request: A contemporary photography gallery called Intervals. Black and white only, Helvetica only, no animation. Make historical photographs the main experience, with an exhibition introduction, selected works, artist information and an exhibition enquiry. No invented awards or sales claims.
craft_floor: Header: one row, 52-88px tall on desktop and 56-76px on mobile; logo 24-40px high on the left, 4-6 nav links of 15-16px at weight 500 with 24-40px between them, the primary action on the right at the header's button size. Phone or hours sit in that row or the footer; no utility bar stacked above the nav. Mark the current link with a 2px underline 6px below the text; a sticky header turns opaque after the first scroll, never taller.

Primary button: 40-56px tall, horizontal padding 20-32px (about twice the vertical), label 15-17px at weight 600 in sentence or title case with tracking 0-0.02em, at most one drawn SVG icon of 16-20px set 8px from the label. The secondary action matches its height, radius and padding as an outline (1-1.5px) or ghost; one button shape and radius on the whole page, 44px minimum hit area everywhere.
Button states: author hover, :active, disabled and :focus-visible feedback without movement. Use a visible 2px focus ring with 3:1 contrast; do not change the control's size or hide its label.

Type scale: at most 10 distinct font sizes each carry 2% or more of the text on a desktop render, each step at least 1.2x the one below; body 17-22px at line-height 1.5-1.65; headings at line-height 1.0-1.15. The h1 tops out at 168px on desktop (set with clamp()), and display sizes of 48px and up track -0.02 to -0.04em, never tighter than -0.05em; body text keeps tracking at 0.
Measure: prose never runs past 78 characters a line (cap paragraphs at 60-68ch with max-width); h1 lines stay under 20ch and h2 under 24ch; no centred paragraph runs past three lines.

Spacing rhythm: use a coherent scale suited to density and content. Group related controls tightly and separate different tasks clearly. Preserve incumbent tokens; do not impose fixed section padding or an arbitrary 4/8px scale on every project.

Section heads: one heading per section (one h2, or the h1 in the hero) and at most one lead paragraph of 40 words or fewer. No stacked pile of label, heading, accent-coloured second heading and paragraph; a second voice goes in the body, not the head.

Composition: choose section forms from the content and reading order. Repeated rows, equal cards and consistent app panels are useful when people compare equivalent items. Vary composition only when it improves hierarchy; no minimum number of layout kinds.

Hero: establish the subject, dominant visual relationship and useful next action. Let the actual content determine the number of pictures, amount of copy and first-screen balance; no mandatory picture or fixed text-block quota.

Imagery: preserve the complete composition of collection works with intrinsic sizing or object-fit: contain. Use whitespace deliberately around differing aspect ratios. Keep artist, title, date and source readable; cropping requires an explicitly labelled detail view.

Colour: respect pinned brand colours and monochrome constraints. Assign clear roles to grounds, text, actions and status; choose saturation and colour area from the concept, without an accent-area quota. Body and secondary text need 4.5:1 contrast, large text 3:1.

Icons: one drawn SVG set at one stroke weight (1.5 or 2px) and one size per context (16, 20 or 24px), coloured with currentColor. Never a Unicode arrow, check mark, star or emoji standing in for an icon.

Motion: none. Render essential content in its final visible state; no entrance, hover movement, autoplay or signature animation. Focus and state changes remain clear without movement, including under prefers-reduced-motion.

Footer: brand and one-line description, two or three link groups and the contact block, four columns at most on desktop; group titles 13-14px at weight 600 in sentence case; links 15-16px with 10-12px between rows; a bottom bar for legal and copyright at 13-14px; 64px or more of top padding.

Browser surfaces: ::selection and focus rings use the palette; link underlines sit 3-4px below the text at 1-2px thickness; tables and figures use tabular numerals; no unthemed default blue links anywhere.
Editorial: a real reading column (60-68ch) with a serif or a strong grotesk at 18-21px; pictures run full-bleed or in the column, never as thumbnails in cards.

design_critique.note: Stylistic devices are not defects by themselves. Diagnose the actual composition, not a list of banned looks.
